v25_precedence_rules.purpose: Preserve high recall while excluding only well-supported ordinary handoffs.

stable_handoff_exclusions.rule: If the target directly answers the preceding Agent's request for a choice, factual parameter, credential, project identity, file, URL, usage estimate, approval, or other input, output DO_NOT_RETAIN unless the same target also reports a concrete problem in existing Agent-instantiated state.

A user-owned external project, template, bot, file, or prior version does not become Agent-instantiated merely because the user selects it as future input. Selecting or supplying such an artifact is ordinary continuation.

If the user explicitly says the current version is correct or acceptable and then asks to document, remember, reuse, export, or apply an already-approved candidate, treat this as successful continuation rather than state reconstruction.

recall_safeguards.rule: “The current/delivered version differs from the original/reference” is explicit mismatch evidence, not a preference revision, when the Agent transformed or reproduced that artifact.

If the preceding trace shows the Agent actively testing, repairing, packaging, or validating the current modified application, a user's contemporaneous report of a crash, unexpected exit, or runtime failure is related state evidence even when that exact symptom was not mentioned by the Agent.

A concrete target-internal correction of an observable current artifact may remain RETAIN_POSSIBLE when preceding state context is absent. Do not require the target to use the words failure, wrong, or bug.

v25_precedence_rules.final_check: Exclude only when one of the stable handoff rules clearly applies or when the v2.3 ordered gates fail. Do not infer successful continuation merely because the target is concise.
